message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 130, "amount_cents": 8178}, {"order_id": 133, "amount_cents": 6783}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Start by checking the refunds table so I can compare it against the refunds Alpha reported before paying anyone.
The refunds table matches the two refunds Alpha reported (order 130 for 8178 and order 133 for 6783), so I can proceed. Next I need the order list to find which customers to pay.
The refunds table matches what Alpha reported. The customers in the order list are acme, birch, and cobalt, so I'll get each one's net balance before recording any payout.

Acme's net balance is 28879. Check: orders 17595 + 26245 = 43840, minus refunds 8178 + 6783 = 14961, gives 28879, which matches. Rather than doing that arithmetic to decide anything, I'll just use the tool figure, so next I'll record acme's payout.
Acme's payout is recorded. Birch is the next customer in the order list, so I'll get Birch's net balance from the tool before recording anything for them.
Birch's net balance is 70733. Its orders are 37666 + 33067 = 70733 and it has no refunds, so the tool figure is consistent. I'll record Birch's payout.
Acme and birch are paid. The only customer left in the order list is cobalt, so I'll get cobalt's net balance from the tool before recording its payout.
Cobalt's net balance is 16841, which matches its orders (10547 + 6294) with no refunds. All three customers now have balances, so I'll record cobalt's payout.
All three customers in the order list (acme, birch, cobalt) have been paid their net balances from the tool, and every record_payout returned ok. The batch is complete.
